case1.title: Evidence supports the claim
case1.claim_text: We reduced routine gas flaring by 40% by 2023 from 2012 levels.

analysis.interval_note: Residual bootstrap around the fitted annual trend. It describes scatter around that trend and carries no analytical coverage guarantee, so it is not a calibrated confidence interval. Its empirical coverage was measured separately and is reported with each verdict.

region_labels.0: meets or beats the claimed reduction
region_labels.1: fell, but by less than claimed

analysis.decision_margin_kind: heuristic: distance from the nearest decision boundary, in interval half-widths. Not a probability and not calibrated.

case1.evidence_ceiling: Single-instrument consistency only: the result is not corroborated by a different sensor.

interval_calibration.note: Empirical coverage measured leave-one-field-out. The interval is not analytically calibrated; this is how often it actually contained the realised change in testing.

case2.claim_text: We reduced routine gas flaring by 25% from 2019 levels.

analysis.decision_margin_kind: heuristic: distance from the nearest decision boundary, in interval half-widths. Not a probability and not calibrated.

case2.evidence_ceiling: No conclusion can be drawn from the available observations.
